scope: kernel_experiment survey cases marked uncertain or reviewed for dataset fit after flow annotation
decision_basis: Whether the case can be represented as two Linux kernel execution contexts with function-level entries and a concrete bug path for the thread-contract storyline.

exclude_candidates.reason: Deterministic sparse phy-index NULL dereference. The patch maps wcid->phy_idx through mt76_dev_phy(); it does not repair a missing synchronization/order between two concurrent kernel contexts.

The patch reverts a shmem_getattr() lock workaround due tmpfs-over-NFS deadlock, but the available CVE evidence does not identify the concrete NFS-side kernel entry/call chain. Expanding into fs/nfs would be speculative without an external trace or reproducer.
The peer is an external MHI host/hardware observer of MMIO-visible ring state, not a second Linux kernel execution context in source.

The visible KCSAN pair is sk_backlog.tail in tcp_recvmsg, while the patch annotates sk_rcvbuf/sk_sndbuf reads in sk_add_backlog callers. The report/patch mismatch makes it unsuitable as ground truth for the patched concurrency behavior.

reviewed_keep_cases.reason: Can be modeled as two rtl_pci_probe executions: a failed first probe leaves a freed rtl_priv list node in a global list, and a later probe manipulates the same list. The unused check_buddy_priv hook is not needed for the confirmed path.
